questions.q: In Spanish, where does a color word go?
options: Before the noun, the same as English
It does not matter where it goes
Only at the very end of the sentence
questions.explanation: The describing word follows the noun: un cuaderno rojo, una casa roja. 'Una roja casa' is not how Spanish works.
Claro (light) and oscuro (dark) come after the color and never change their ending: verde claro, azul claro.

questions.q: 'La casa es ___.' The house is red. Which word is correct?
questions.explanation: Casa is a 'la' word, so rojo changes to roja: la casa roja. With an 'el' word it stays rojo: el cuaderno rojo.

questions.q: What is unusual about the word arcoíris (rainbow)?
options: It ends in -s but it is an 'el' word
It is always used in the plural
It can never be described with a color
questions.explanation: It is el arcoíris, not 'la arcoíris' — and the plural is still los arcoíris, with no extra -s.

questions.q: 'El sol es ___.' The sun is bright and shiny. Which word fits?
questions.explanation: Brillante means bright or shiny. It ends in -e, so it never changes its ending.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly describes a favorite object?
options: Mi mochila es bonita y morada.
Mi mochila es bonito y morado.
questions.explanation: Mochila is a 'la' word, so both bonita and morada take -a, and they come after the noun: Mi mochila es bonita y morada.
